beats.speaker: tilly
beats.voiceover: Saturn is wild. Nine Earths could line up across it.

beats.speaker: tilly
beats.voiceover: Split it open and there's no ground at all. Just gas and liquid, crushed around a dense core.

beats.speaker: tilly
beats.voiceover: It's so light for its size, it would float in water, if you found a tub big enough.

beats.speaker: tilly
beats.voiceover: A day there lasts about ten and a half hours.

beats.speaker: tilly
beats.voiceover: Its north pole has a storm shaped like a hexagon.

beats.speaker: tilly
beats.voiceover: Its rings reach hundreds of thousands of kilometres out, but the main ones are often about ten metres thick.

views.subtitle: typical thickness of the main rings

beats.speaker: tilly
beats.voiceover: Cassini studied it for thirteen years. Saturn still surprises us.

claims.claim: Saturn is about 9 times wider than Earth (diameter about 116,000 km vs Earth's 12,742 km), so about nine Earths could line up across it; Earth's diameter is about 0.11 of Saturn's.
claims.source: NASA Science, Saturn facts, https://science.nasa.gov/saturn/facts/ ; Canadian Space Agency, Saturn, https://asc-csa.gc.ca/eng/astronomy/solar-system/saturn.asp (116,464 km, 'about 9 Earths')
claims.note: Shown as '≈ 9 Earths wide' and as an Earth disc at 0.11 of Saturn's size.

claims.claim: Saturn has no solid surface: it is mostly hydrogen and helium gas, with liquid hydrogen and liquid metallic hydrogen deeper down around a dense core.
claims.source: NASA Science, Saturn facts, https://science.nasa.gov/saturn/facts/ ; Sky & Telescope, 'Surprising science from Cassini's Grand Finale', https://skyandtelescope.org/astronomy-news/surprising-science-from-cassinis-grand-finale/
claims.note: Layer sizes in the cutaway are illustrative. Cassini data suggest the core may be diffuse, so it is labelled only 'Dense core'.

claims.claim: Saturn's average density (about 0.69 g/cm³) is less than water's, so it would float if there were water enough to hold it.
claims.source: NASA Goddard (archived), https://science.gsfc.nasa.gov/attic/huygensgcms/Saturn.htm ; BBC Sky at Night, https://www.skyatnightmagazine.com/space-science/saturn-could-float-on-water
claims.note: A thought experiment; said with 'if you found a tub big enough'. Shown about 69% under water.

claims.claim: A day on Saturn lasts about 10 hours 33 minutes (Cassini ring-seismology measurement, 2019).
claims.source: NASA Science, Saturn facts, https://science.nasa.gov/saturn/facts/ ; Mental Floss, https://mentalfloss.com/article/501981/9-essential-facts-about-saturn
claims.note: 10 h 33 min 38 s; said as 'about ten and a half hours'.

claims.claim: Saturn's north pole has a long-lasting six-sided (hexagonal) storm pattern.
Saturn's ring system extends up to about 282,000 km (175,000 miles) from the planet, yet the main rings are typically only about 10 metres (30 feet) thick.
claims.source: NASA Science, Saturn facts, https://science.nasa.gov/saturn/facts/ ('extends up to 175,000 miles (282,000 kilometers) from the planet, yet the vertical height is typically about 30 feet (10 meters) in the main rings')

claims.claim: NASA's Cassini spacecraft orbited and studied Saturn for about 13 years, from 2004 to 2017.
claims.source: Universe Today, https://www.universetoday.com/articles/what-cassinis-grand-finale-taught-us-about-saturns-interior ; NASA Cassini mission pages

publish.description: It would float in water, its rings are about ten metres thick and its north pole has a hexagon. Strange facts about Saturn.
